newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE white sugar turns lower, nearby spread focus.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE white sugar turns lower, nearby spread focus.

text.p: White sugar futures were content to hover just above intraday lows on Wednesday with the nearby March/May spread dominating turnover ahead of the spot expiry, traders said.

After opening above $6.00 as a result of a late rally on Tuesday, the spread contracted to trade between $4.50 and $5.00 as all positions lost ground amid interest from trade, broker and commission house players.

Traders said while the spread was the prevailing feature of the session, they also pointed to outright business concluded on spot March and March/March purchases at $72 which pushed the value out to $73.
"There's been a good mixture of everything," said one trader.

At 1645 GMT March was down $1.80 at $306.30 and May down $1.80 at $301.80. Volume was boosted by against actuals trades and reached a hefty 3,904 lots, most of which was equally split between the front two months.
"It's all being tidied up before expiry tomorrow...but in the last day of trading anything can happen," said another trader.
In physical news, Sri Lanka bought 12,500 tonnes of white sugar from Gill & Duffus at $336.90 per tonne. Specified delivery dates are March 15/April 5.
Belarus recently bought 260,000 tonnes of raw sugar from Brazil, which when refined should bring the national 1996/97 white sugar output to 372,000 tonnes.
Paris futures positions were also weaker in a total volume of 1,663 lots.
March was down $2.00 at $304.60 and May down $1.10 at $301.50.
